help.title: Guide
help.intro: bacuy-y is a page of text: each line is a task. You type, and everything is saved on this device right away, online or not; when there is a connection, it syncs with your other devices.

start.p1: Enter makes a new line below (or splits the line, if the cursor is in the middle). The “+ Add line” button, under the last line, adds a new one at the end from anywhere. Enter at the start of a line adds an empty line above, and the line keeps everything it had. Backspace at the start joins it with the line above; on an empty line, it deletes it.
start.p2: The box at the start of each line marks it as done; what happens depends on the type (see below). The ⋯ button opens the line's panel, with the rest of its details.
start.p3: Suggestions appear as you type: marks, and lines you wrote before (completed ones too). Enter or Tab complete a mark; ↓ and Enter, or a tap, copy a line.

marks.intro: Marks are short words inside the line that fill in its details. They are left out of the title and shown highlighted. They work in Spanish and English, with or without accents. An underlined mark was not recognized.
marks.flag: A flag (category). You can add several. A subflag is written on its own or with its path. A line with a flag becomes active and counts in the priority.
marks.type: The line's type. Without a mark, it is an action.
marks.date: A date: today, tomorrow, a weekday, 31/12 or 2026-12-31. When you leave the line it is fixed to an exact date. What it means depends on the type.
marks.frequency: How often it repeats: daily, weekly or monthly. Only for repeating actions and habits; a line with a frequency and no type is a repeating action.

types.intro: Each type behaves differently when ticked, and its panel shows only what fits it: its own details, the schedule if it repeats (or the review, for attitudes and skills), description, flags, hide and feedback (not for gratitude or expirations).
types.frequencyYes: yes; in the panel you can pick which weekdays, which day of the month and what time

ACTION.what: Something to do once. It is the default type.
ACTION.start: When you type it. Without a flag it is a draft; with one, active.
ACTION.use: It stays on the page until you tick it. With @date it has a deadline.
ACTION.end: Ticking it completes it and moves it to Completed. Unticking it there puts it back in its place.

REPETITIVE_ACTION.what: Something done again and again (watering, paying a fee). It can have a target number of times.
REPETITIVE_ACTION.start: When you type it with !repeat or a ~frequency.
REPETITIVE_ACTION.use: Ticking it counts one more time (times done) and hides it.
REPETITIVE_ACTION.repeat: It comes back by itself on the next day picked in the panel; if none is picked, 1 day, 7 days or a month after you tick it. Meanwhile it is in Hidden.
REPETITIVE_ACTION.end: Completed when it reaches the target number of times, or when you complete it in the panel. Without a target it repeats forever.

HABIT.what: A habit you want to build. It keeps a streak.
HABIT.start: When you type it with !habit, usually with a ~frequency.
HABIT.use: Ticking it adds one to the streak and hides it.
HABIT.repeat: It comes back by itself like a repeating action. The streak is not reset by itself if you miss a day; you can reset it in the panel.
HABIT.end: When it reaches the target streak it offers to mark it as formed (completed). Also from the panel.

ATTITUDE.what: A way of being or reacting you want to grow, with an affirmation that sums it up.
ATTITUDE.start: When you type it with !attitude. In the panel you can add an affirmation.
ATTITUDE.use: Tick it when you have kept it in mind: it asks “How did it go?” Well or Badly, and hides until its next review.
ATTITUDE.repeat: It comes back at 03:00 on its day: 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks, 1, 2, 3 and 6 months. “Well” moves one step up (longer), “Badly” one down (sooner). If you skip a review, it waits for you. A ~frequency is not used.
ATTITUDE.end: “Well” on the last step (6 months) marks it internalized and moves it to Completed. You can also complete or archive it in the panel.

SKILL.what: Something you are learning, with its level and the resources you use.
SKILL.start: When you type it with !skill. In the panel, its level and the resources you use.
SKILL.use: Tick it when you practise it: it asks “How did it go?” Well or Badly, and hides until its next review. You raise the level in the panel.
SKILL.repeat: Like an attitude: back at 03:00 after 1 day, 3 days, 1 week… up to 6 months, up with “Well” and down with “Badly”. If you skip a review, it waits for you.
SKILL.end: “Well” on the last step (6 months) counts it as mastered and moves it to Completed. Also from the panel, or archive it.

MOMENTO.what: An event with a date: a birthday, a trip, an appointment.
MOMENTO.start: When you type it with !moment and the event's @date.
MOMENTO.use: Always on the page, with a star instead of the box.
MOMENTO.repeat: No. For something yearly, like a birthday, write a new moment with the next date.
MOMENTO.end: Not completed: once it has passed, archive it in the panel. It is not archived by itself.

GRATITUDE.what: Something or someone you are grateful for. When completed it goes to the Journal.
GRATITUDE.start: When you type it with !gratitude, or automatically every day if you turn it on in Settings (this browser).
GRATITUDE.use: Ticking it opens the panel to write the notes (and, if you like, who it is for).
GRATITUDE.repeat: Each entry is unique; the automatic one creates a new one per scheduled time (not for days you did not open the app).
GRATITUDE.end: “Save & complete” (notes required) takes it to the Journal.

EXPIRATION.what: Something that expires and must be renewed: passport, insurance, licence.
EXPIRATION.start: When you type it with !expires and the expiry @date.
EXPIRATION.use: Shows the days left (amber inside its warning, red when overdue). It waits off the page and shows up only its lead days before (30 by default, in its panel), at 3:00; from then it is also in Priority and rises as the date nears. Meanwhile it is on Expirations.
EXPIRATION.repeat: Renewed with a new date, it waits on Expirations again until the next warning.
EXPIRATION.end: Not completed: “Archive without renewing” takes it off the page. Restoring it makes it pending again.

statusItems.DRAFT: Just written, no flags. It can already be ticked.
statusItems.ACTIVE: Has at least one flag; counts in the priority view.
statusItems.INACTIVE: Paused (from the panel): stays on the page, in italics, without a box.
statusItems.COMPLETED: Done: it is in Completed (or in the Journal, for gratitude).
statusItems.ARCHIVED: Kept off the page, in Archived; it can be restored.

views.page: To do: your page. It can be filtered by flag; a new line typed while filtered gets that flag.
views.hidden: Hidden: what you hid from the panel (until a date and time, or until you show it), repeating actions and habits done for now, and attitudes and skills waiting for their next review. Shows when each comes back. A search box at the top finds any part of the text (case and accents don't matter).
views.expirations: Expirations: everything that expires, soonest first, with the days left and whether it is on the page or when it shows up. Renew from here.
views.completed: Completed: what is done, newest first, grouped by day.
views.archived: Archived: what you kept off the page.
views.priority: Priority: active lines ordered by their flags' weight; lines whose cron time is within the hour and expirations coming up rise. Read only; tapping one takes you to it.
views.flags: Flags: create, arrange and weight your categories. Sibling weights add up to 100.
views.settings: Settings: language, theme, install the app and your account (sign out).

keys.backspace: At the start: join with the line above

lifecycle.title: Life cycle of any line
items: It is born when you type it, as a draft. With its first flag it becomes active; remove them all and it is a draft again.
The page shows drafts, active and paused lines that are not hidden. Priority shows only active lines (with a flag) that are not hidden.
Pausing (in the panel) keeps it on the page in italics, without a box and out of Priority, until you reactivate it.

Hiding takes it off the page until a date and time, or until you show it; it is listed on Hidden. Fastest: swiping it right (or Ctrl+Shift+H, or the moon next to ⋯) hides it until tomorrow 8:00; swiping further lets you choose. Before 3:00, “tomorrow 8:00” means this morning.
Completing moves it to Completed (gratitude, to the Journal). Reactivating it brings it back to the page.
Archiving keeps it off the page, in Archived, without completing it. Restoring puts it at the end of the page.
Deleting it (in the panel, or Backspace on an empty line) removes it on all your devices. If it had text, a notice lets you undo it for a few seconds.
The day starts at 3:00: until then the night counts as the day before (for “today”, “tomorrow”, days left, what comes back “tomorrow” and Completed).

review.question: How did it go?
review.overridesFrequency: Attitudes and skills are reviewed at intervals that adapt to how it goes: the ~frequency is not used.
review.dueNow: Due for review: tick it and say how it went.

expirations.title: Expirations
expirations.intro: Everything that expires (passport, insurance, licences…), soonest first. Each one waits off the page and shows up only when its warning starts (the lead days in its panel, 30 by default), at 3:00.
expirations.empty: No expirations. Type a line with !expires and a date, e.g. “Passport !expires @2027-03-01”.
expirations.waitingToast: Expires later on: it will show up on the page on {{date}}.
